opportunity.title: Scalable GEOINT Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support
opportunity.description: Request for Proposal W50NH9-27-R-A006 for Scalable Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture IT Contractor Manpower Equivalent support for U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM). Proposals due Nov 13, 2026 with a proposal validity of at least 240 days. Period of performance: one 30-day transition-in, a 12-month base, four 12-month options and one six-month option. Estimated award date Jan 11, 2027. Primarily time and materials, evaluated on a best value trade-off basis.

rationale.point: Company can only staff work in Arizona, but the solicitation lists Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD as a place of performance, creating a fundamental geographic mismatch.

The opportunity is issued full and open with no small-business set-aside, indicating intense competition from large firms, while the company has only four staff, no clearances, no SOC 2, and this would be its first federal bid.

The requirement is for scalable GEOINT architecture IT contractor manpower equivalent support under a time-and-materials, best-value contract, which likely demands specialized expertise, clearances, and capacity far beyond the company's two small state-agency data-entry projects ($250K and $180K).

risks: Cannot meet place-of-performance requirement in Maryland
No federal past performance or relevant GEOINT architecture experience
No personnel clearances or SOC 2 certification
Extreme size and experience mismatch against large-firm competitors in full-and-open competition
Median top award value ($152M) dwarfs company's largest project ($250K)
nextSteps: Target opportunities with Arizona place of performance
Pursue small-business set-aside contracts to build federal past performance
Consider subcontracting to gain relevant experience and clearances
Invest in certifications (e.g., SOC 2) and clearance sponsorship if pursuing federal work
